To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
frequent Internet users tend to be more lonely and to have deviant (idiosyncratic) values, and also tend to lack emotional and social skills.
Internet use is related to emotional intelligence (EI), loneliness, idiosyncrasy, and work-life imbalance.
frequent users of the Internet have poorer emotional intelligence, are lonelier and more likely to hold deviant values, but are not different in terms of personality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between Internet addiction, social skills, and personality.
the relationship between Internet use, social and emotional skills, and adjustment.
the study of personality, emotional intelligence and Internet use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the Internet, in itself, is neither a good nor bad thing.
Internet addiction is not associated with a specific personality profile, but with a tendency to be lonely and to have idiosyncrasy.
Internet use is associated with some aspects of social skills, personality, emotional intelligence and adjustment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

frequent Internet users are lonely and have a low level of EI, which is related to the fact that they are not able to manage the social environment in which they live, and are therefore more likely to seek a substitute in the virtual world.
frequent Internet use is related to social and emotional deficits, which may in part explain its negative impact on the individual's social adjustment.
Internet use, social skills, and adjustment are related to each other in complex ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Internet is not a panacea, and that it can be used in a way that can lead to social isolation and loneliness.

Internet use is related to a number of social and psychological characteristics that may be important for the understanding of the social consequences of Internet use, but that personality does not seem to be related to Internet use.
the more people use the Internet, the lonelier, the less socially skilled, and less emotionally intelligent they tend to be.
